Punjab govt seeks Rangers deployment in Rawalpindi, three other districts until Oct 5
items.description: The Punjab government has requested the federal government to deploy Rangers in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali districts from Sept 22 to Oct 5 to assist the provincial police in maintaining law and order amid an expected protest on Sept 27. The request comes as the Kissan Ittehad and PTI have announced long marches and sit-ins in Islamabad in the coming week. PTI has announced a long march on Sept 27 to press for the release of its founder, Imran Khan. The letter, a copy of which is available with Dawn , said Rangers had been requested for deployment in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali from Sept 22 to Oct 5. According to a letter sent by the Punjab Home Department to the Ministry of Interior and Narcotics Control, three companies of the Pakistan Rangers have been sought for deployment in Rawalpindi, including one for Rawalpindi city and two for Taxila. Five Rangers wings have been sought for Attock, while Jhelum and Mianwali have each been allocated one company. The deployment is proposed under Article 245 of the Constitution of Pakistan, 1973, Sections 4 and 5 of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, and Sections 7(b) and 10 of the Pakistan Rangers Ordinance, 1959. The letter said the matter was discussed threadbare at the 59th meeting of the Standing Committee of the Cabinet on Law & Order (SCCLO) of the Punjab government, held on Sept 20. The meeting considered the situational review presented by police authorities, the orders of the Islamabad High Court (IHC) in Writ Petition No. 4421/2026, and instructions issued by the S&GAD, Government of Punjab, through a letter dated Sept 19, 2026, it stated. “After due consideration, it was authorised that the requisition be sent to the ministry of interior, for requisition of troops ensuring law and order in the districts mentioned above,” the letter stated. The letter asked the ministry to take further necessary action and intimate the Punjab Home Department accordingly. Section 144 declared Separately, Section 144 has been enforced across Punjab from Sept 23 to Oct 5, with a complete ban imposed on the assembly, processions, or gathering of five or more people in public places, on highways, or in open spaces across Punjab. Inciting people to unlawful assembly is also prohibited. The ban does not apply, however, to wedding ceremonies, funeral prayers, burials, or gatherings at mosques and other places of worship. Courts of law, government or semi-governmental organisations’ official duties, and events held with official permission from the deputy commissioner of the concerned district are also exempt. A complete ban has also been imposed on carrying or displaying weapons of any kind in public places, according to an order issued by the Punjab Home Department. This ban exempts personnel of law enforcement agencies (LEAs), intelligence agencies (IAs) and security agencies on official duty. The order, a copy of which is available with Dawn , said that Section 144 was imposed in view of serious threats to public peace, tranquility, and the lives and property of citizens across Punjab. “Multiple threat alerts have been received from IAs regarding possible terrorist activities being planned by such hostile agencies by employing suicide bombers, Vehicle Bound Improvised Explosive Devises (VBIEDs) and target killings during large public gatherings across Punjab to create mayhem, social unrest and disrupt public peace and tranquility,” it said, noting that “gatherings, rallies, public meetings, sit-ins, processions, and demonstrations” could become potential soft targets for terrorist attacks. The order has been enforced immediately and is to remain in effect for 13 days. The department has also sent a letter to the interior ministry requesting mobile and internet services at specific locations in Rawalpindi and Attock to be downgraded or jammed from the morning of Sept 27. 2G, 3G and 4G networks are requested to be jammed at specified locations in Rawalpindi, from Barahma Bahtar to M-1, Gango, Ahata, Taxila City, Wah Saddar, Thalian, and Chakri. It was also requested to downgrade mobile and internet services throughout Attock district. The decision to disrupt mobile and internet signals was made on the request of police to maintain law and order, according to the Home Department on social media, which also requested that “further necessary action may kindly be taken accordingly”. “The protection of the lives and property of the public is the top priority of the Government of Punjab,” the department’s spokesperson said. Preparations in the Rawalpindi Division and the federal capital territory to maintain security and deal with any emergency situation are in full swing in light of the potential long march by the PTI and other protests in Islamabad. More than 22,000 security personnel led by eight DIGs will be deployed in the federal capital and over 30,000 in the Attock district, which connects Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with Punjab. In Aug, the federal government authorised the deployment of three companies of the Pakistan Army in Rawalpindi for six months to perform “sensitive security duties” and respond to any unforeseen situation. The deployment was approved more than a month before the planned PTI march towards Islamabad. The party claims that the Sept 27 long march could draw around two million participants. District administrations in Punjab have previously sought army assistance under Article 245 during Muharram, election periods, and times of heightened terror alerts. With the deployment approved for an initial period of six months “with immediate effect”, the army units will be placed at the disposal of the Rawalpindi district administration and will perform duties as assigned by the civilian authorities.

items.title: P.L.O. Lumumba: Nkrumah foresaw Africa’s vulnerability without unity – P.L.O. Lumumba
items.description: Renowned Pan-Africanist and anti-corruption crusader Professor P.L.O. Lumumba has said Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah foresaw that Africa’s failure to unite would leave the continent vulnerable to domination, humiliation and external influence. According to Prof. Lumumba, Nkrumah possessed exceptional foresight and understood as far back as the 1960s that a fragmented Africa would struggle to protect its interests and address challenges affecting its people. Speaking in an interview with JoyPrime’s Isreal Laryea, Prof. Lumumba said Nkrumah’s vision remained relevant as the continent continued to grapple with conflicts, humanitarian crises and other challenges. “Nkrumah would have been celebrating his 117th year and what one must remember about the Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah is that he had the foresight of a prophet,” he said. He said Nkrumah recognised that an Africa without meaningful unity would be vulnerable to domination and undermining by external forces. “He was able to see an Africa that was not united would be dominated, would be undermined, would be humiliated, and I dare say if you look at all the critical sectors of human relations, Africa is being dominated, Africa is being humiliated, and Africa is being disregarded,” Prof. Lumumba said. Prof. Lumumba argued that Africa could have been in a different position today had the continent and the wider international community paid greater attention to Nkrumah’s call for African unity. He said the former Ghanaian leader envisaged a strong Africa capable of contributing meaningfully to global affairs while protecting the interests and dignity of its people. “If Africa would have listened to Kwame Nkrumah, if only the world would have listened to Kwame Nkrumah that you needed a strong African… it would be different,” he said. The Pan-Africanist said Nkrumah’s concerns about the consequences of division had become particularly evident in the area of peace and security. He pointed to the numerous conflicts on the continent, arguing that they continue to undermine peace and create humanitarian situations that African countries often struggle to resolve. “As we talk now, there are almost 40 conflicts in the continent of Africa which undermine peace, which creates humanitarian situations which cannot be handled by Africans,” he said. Prof. Lumumba stressed that Nkrumah had anticipated such difficulties decades ago. “The Osagyefo had foreseen that as early as the 1960s,” he added. His comments form part of renewed reflections on Nkrumah’s Pan-African legacy as Ghana commemorates what would have been the former President’s 117th birthday.

items.title: ‘Darkness has taken over,’ residents lament as vandals strip 168 lights
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — Residents and motorists along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway have raised the alarm over the theft of more than 168 solar-powered streetlights installed along the five-kilometre Longbridge section of the highway. The development has plunged parts of the corridor around Warewa, Wawa, Arepo and Magboro into darkness, heightening concerns about the safety of motorists and residents, particularly at night. The solar-powered streetlights were installed in 2025 as part of efforts to improve visibility and address security concerns along the busy highway. However, many of the poles, LED fittings and solar panels have reportedly been systematically removed, leaving significant portions of the highway unlit. The affected stretch has in the past been associated with reports of highway robbery and attacks on motorists, particularly those whose vehicles break down at night. Residents fear that the renewed darkness could provide cover for criminals and expose stranded motorists to attacks before help arrives. At highway speeds, the absence of lighting could also make stalled vehicles, road debris and other hazards more difficult for motorists to detect. The Lagos-Ibadan Expressway is a major transport corridor linking Lagos with other parts of the country, carrying commuters, commercial vehicles and heavy-duty trucks daily. ‘We’re back in the dark ages’ A resident and public interest analyst, Mr Nelson Ekujumi, condemned the vandalisation of the public infrastructure, describing it as a threat to public safety. “The vandalisation of public assets like the solar-powered streetlights on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway is highly condemnable. “I was shocked that the whole place, which was formerly lit up, has been thrown back into darkness. “Agents of darkness perpetrate their evil acts under the cover of night,” Ekujumi said. He urged the authorities to ensure that anyone arrested over the vandalism was prosecuted in accordance with the law. It was observed that some streetlights at the extreme ends of the bridge, where traffic and pedestrian movements are more frequent, remained intact, while several central sections had been stripped of their lighting equipment. A resident identified simply as Lucky said the removal of the lights had revived fears over security along the corridor. “Before the installations, there were constant cases of robbery, kidnapping, and attacks on motorists, especially those whose vehicles broke down. “Now, all of that is returning,” he said. Another resident of Arepo, Hakeem Olawepo, said the situation had remained unchanged since the streetlights began disappearing. “Nothing has changed since the day they started removing them,” Olawepo lamented. “That is why you no longer see streetlights on the bridge. The darkness has completely taken over, leaving room for unscrupulous elements to carry out their nefarious activities.” Publisher of Pentouch.com.ng, Ayodele Lawal, also expressed concern over the development. “The vandalisation of solar-powered lights is very disturbing and, if something urgent is not done, it can lead to insecurity of lives and property,” Lawal said. Police arrest four suspects The Ogun State Police Command has confirmed the arrest of at least four suspects allegedly linked to the theft and vandalisation of infrastructure along the corridor. The suspects were identified as Simon David, Yinusa Garba, Fawas Suleiman and Tunde Tobiloba. According to the information provided by the authorities, the suspects were arrested and charged over alleged offences ranging from nighttime asset stripping and metal theft to vandalism of highway infrastructure and possession of cut steel poles and other accessories. However, surveillance efforts along the corridor were reportedly affected by an accident involving a police patrol vehicle. The Federal Controller of Works in Ogun State, Michael Komolafe, said the patrol vehicle was rammed by another vehicle, leaving an officer injured and disrupting police surveillance. “I met with the police, and the DPO assured us their men were always on patrol. But he later informed me that their vehicle was rammed and damaged, and an officer was hospitalised. The vandals immediately took advantage of that gap in police presence,” Komolafe said. He said replacing the stolen lights without first putting adequate security measures in place would expose the infrastructure to renewed vandalism. “Efforts towards replacement are not there yet. Even if we replace them, we must first ensure they cannot be vandalised again. “Otherwise, we are simply working for the vandals,” he said. Authorities move to curb vandalism The Ogun State Police Command and traffic management authorities, including the Traffic Compliance and Enforcement Corps (TRACE), have reportedly redeployed operational personnel to maintain a continuous presence along the affected stretch. The move is aimed at deterring further vandalism and the activities of suspected scrap-metal buyers. The Federal Ministry of Works is also said to be considering anti-theft measures before replacing the stolen equipment, including stronger anti-tamper fastenings and protective structural enclosures. Meanwhile, stakeholders and civil society organisations have called for the installation of solar-powered closed-circuit television cameras linked to police control centres to enable real-time monitoring of public infrastructure along the corridor. The post ‘Darkness has taken over,’ residents lament as vandals strip 168 lights appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Un agent d’opérateur Télécom arrêté pour vol de 707 000 FCFA via Orange Money
items.description: Grâce au détournement d'une carte SIM, un employé d'une société de téléphonie a vidé le compte Mobile Money d'un usager avant d'être traqué et déféré au parquet par la Sûreté urbaine de Rufisque, au Sénégal, selon une annonce de la police, ce mercredi 23 septembre 2026. Un loup dans la bergerie. À Rufisque, au Sénégal, les policiers de la Sûreté urbaine ont mis fin aux agissements d'un agent de téléphonie mobile spécialisé dans le piratage interne. L'affaire prend sa source le 22 août 2026, lorsqu'un utilisateur constate la spoliation de son portefeuille électronique. Occupé par des travaux agricoles, ce dernier n'avait pas immédiatement prêté attention à la désactivation brusque de sa puce survenue le 7 août. Ce n'est qu'en rétablissant sa ligne, quinze jours plus tard, qu'il a découvert le pot aux roses: deux opérations frauduleuses exécutées le soir même de la coupure, prélevant un total de 707 000 F CFA (frais compris). Saisis d'une plainte, les enquêteurs ont lancé des réquisitions techniques dont les résultats se sont révélés sans appel. Le suspect utilisait la procédure de «Changement d'abonné» (CA), un mécanisme interne normalement réservé à la réémission de puces pour les clients, afin de prendre le contrôle à distance des numéros ciblés et d'en vider les avoirs. Face aux preuves matérielles réunies par les forces de l'ordre, le mis en cause a rapidement reconnu les faits lors de son audition. Si l'agent indélicat a réussi à restituer la totalité des fonds dérobés avec le soutien de sa famille, le coup de filet n'en reste pas moins sévère sur le plan judiciaire. L’employeur du suspect a lui aussi porté plainte et s'est constitué partie civile, dénonçant une atteinte grave à son image de marque tout en évaluant l'éventuel impact financier global de ces manipulations. Le suspect répond désormais devant la justice d'accès frauduleux à un système informatique, d'usurpation d'avantages économiques et de vols répétés. Cette arrestation remet brutalement en lumière la vulnérabilité des comptes de paiement mobile face aux menaces internes et pose la question de la sécurisation des habilitations au sein des opérateurs Télécom. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Un agent d'opérateur Télécom arrêté pour vol de 707 000 FCFA via Orange Money est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Sunderland penalty against Arsenal incorrect — Premier League panel
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A Premier League panel has unanimously ruled that the penalty awarded to Sunderland against Arsenal was incorrect, vindicating Mikel Arteta’s furious reaction to the decision. Referee John Brooks awarded Sunderland a penalty after penalising Arsenal defender Ezri Konsa for holding Dan Ballard during a corner in the September 12 meeting. David Raya saved Enzo Le Fee’s resulting spot-kick as Arsenal went on to win 2-0. Arteta had strongly contested the decision after the match, with Arsenal subsequently contacting Pro Ref to seek an explanation. The Premier League’s five-person Key Match Incidents panel unanimously disagreed with the on-field decision, according to ESPN. “Although it was a very untidy challenge in which Konsa initially had arms around Ballard, Ballard engages in a holding action which pulls Konsa onto him so they both fall to the floor,” the panel said. However, the panel voted 3-2 in support of VAR Stuart Attwell’s decision not to intervene, saying the incident did not amount to a clear and obvious error. Arteta had said after the match: “[The decision] is not acceptable. I watched it 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how they’d think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. “At this level with all the work we put in, this cannot happen.” The panel is made up of three former players and coaches, one Premier League representative and one representative from Pro Ref. Meanwhile, the panel unanimously agreed that Erling Haaland’s winner in the Manchester derby earlier this month should have been disallowed for offside. Haaland’s goal at Old Trafford on September 13 was allowed to stand after VAR Matt Donohue and his assistant Blake Antrobus determined that the Norwegian striker was onside. However, they failed to send referee Michael Oliver to review Enzo Fernández’s interference with play while in an offside position. Pro Ref chief refereeing officer Howard Webb said Donohue had “tunnel vision” during the incident, with his focus appearing to be on establishing that Haaland was onside and whether Fernández had touched the ball. Webb said Donohue’s assistants, including Antrobus, should have pulled him out of that tunnel. The pair were subsequently stood down from last weekend’s Premier League matches. Pro Ref contacted Manchester United to acknowledge the error and promised a review of its processes following the incident. In its summary published on Wednesday, the panel said: “Fernandez is in an offside position, attempts to play the ball that is close to him, and impacts the ability of the defender and the goalkeeper to play the ball in the process. “A VAR review should have been recommended for a missed subjective offside in the attacking possession phase.” The panel also unanimously backed the decision to send off Manchester City’s Phil Foden in the same game for kicking out at Manchester United’s Bruno Fernandes. However, the panel felt Fernandes’ actions in the incident were worthy of a yellow card. If Oliver had not sent Foden off the field, VAR could have recommended a booking for Fernandes as part of a red-card review of Foden’s conduct. items.title: Alhaji Faisal Abdullah Masud installed as Tema’s first Sariki Zongo
items.description: Alhaji Faisal Abdullah Masud has been installed as Sariki Zongo I of Tema, becoming the first person to officially hold the title in the history of the industrial city. Widely known in Tema as Alhaji Faisal Saltan (Alhaji Netro), his installation represents a significant moment for the numerous Zongo communities spread across Tema Manhean, Tema New Town, Community One, Bankuman, Ashaiman and surrounding areas. For decades, these communities have been home to people from diverse ethnic and cultural backgrounds. The establishment of a unified traditional leadership structure under the Tema Sariki Zongo stool is therefore being seen as an opportunity to strengthen unity, representation and development across the various Zongo communities. The coronation of Alhaji Faisal Abdullah Masud brought together traditional leaders, Islamic authorities, representatives of various ethnic communities and other stakeholders in a celebration of culture, unity and peaceful coexistence. Representatives of communities including Dagomba, Frafra, Hausa, Kusaasi, Mamprusi, Kotokoli, Yoruba and other groups were present at the historic occasion. The event also reflected the long-standing relationship between Muslims and Christians in Tema, with members of both faiths participating in the celebration. The occasion was therefore more than a traditional ceremony. It marked the beginning of a new traditional leadership structure intended to provide a stronger platform for dialogue, cooperation and development within the Zongo communities of Tema. Alhaji Faisal Abdullah Masud combines traditional leadership with extensive experience in business, sports and community development. He is the president of True Democracy F.C., a Division One League team, and the owner of 90’s Lounge. He also serves as CEO of Paramount Empire Trading and Investment Company Limited and Sultan Incorporation. He is additionally involved in the hospitality and agricultural sectors as a hotelier and farmer. His background in entrepreneurship and youth-oriented activities forms an important part of his vision for the development of the Tema Zongo communities, particularly in the areas of employment, skills development and economic empowerment. As the first Sariki Zongo I of Tema, Alhaji Faisal Abdullah Masud has outlined a six-point development agenda focused on building a more united, peaceful and progressive Zongo community. His first priority is unity and peace-building, bringing together the various ethnic groups within the Tema Zongos and promoting dialogue to resolve chieftaincy and community-related disagreements, while strengthening relations with the Tema Traditional Council and government institutions. He also places strong emphasis on youth empowerment and sports development, using his experience in football and business to create opportunities for young people through sports, hospitality, trading, agriculture and other forms of skills development. Education and skills development are another key priority, with plans to support both Islamic and secular education, provide scholarship opportunities, reduce school dropout rates and connect young people to technical and vocational training programmes. On economic empowerment and entrepreneurship, Alhaji Faisal intends to use his business experience to mentor entrepreneurs, support traders and market women, and promote greater financial inclusion within the Zongo communities. His agenda also includes sanitation, health and social welfare through community clean-up exercises, health screening programmes and support for vulnerable members of the community, particularly during Ramadan and Eid. Finally, he is committed to community security and the fight against drug abuse, working with Imams, elders, youth leaders and the Ghana Police Service to address drug abuse, crime and other challenges affecting young people in the Zongo communities.

items.title: Mahama’s UN address to mark 25th by a Ghanaian president
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama’s scheduled address to the 81st United Nations General Assembly on Thursday, 24 September 2026, will be the 25th General Debate address by a Ghanaian president, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. In a social media post tracing Ghana’s presidential appearances at the Assembly, the Ministry said the country’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, delivered the first address on 23 September 1960. Dr Kwame Nkrumah addressing the Assembly in 1960 Mr Mahama’s planned appearance comes 66 years later. The Ministry’s list records 24 presidential addresses up to the 80th session in 2025. Former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo leads with eight addresses between 2017 and 2024. Former Ghanaian President, the late Jerry John Rawlings, at the Assembly in 1998 Former President John Agyekum Kufuor and Mahama have delivered six each, while former President John Evans Atta Mills addressed the General Debate twice. Nkrumah and former President Jerry John Rawlings made one appearance each. According to the post, 38 years passed between Nkrumah’s address and Rawlings’ appearance on 22 September 1998. The ministry stressed that Ghana remained represented at the UN during that period, including by foreign ministers Ako Adjei and Kojo Botsio and other senior officials. Former President John Agyekum Kufuor attended six times Mahama previously addressed the General Debate in 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016 and 2025. His address on Thursday would be his seventh and would bring the total number of presidential addresses listed by the ministry to 25. Former President, the late John Evans Atta Mills, attended twice, in 2009 and 2011 The ministry’s post says seven Ghanaian presidents have addressed the General Debate, but the six presidents it names account for all 24 appearances in its list. Former President Akufo-Addo attended eight times

items.title: ICC convicts ex-CAR rebel leader for crimes against humanity
items.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) on Wednesday convicted former Central African Republic rebel commander Mahamat Said Abdel Kani on four counts of crimes against humanity, including torture and unlawful imprisonment. The 56-year-old was found guilty of overseeing beatings and other forms of mistreatment while serving as head of a detention unit during the Central African Republic’s civil war in 2013. Said, who was wearing a blue sweatshirt and jeans during the proceedings, reportedly shook his head several times as presiding Judge Miatta Maria Samba read out details of the crimes. The ICC, however, acquitted him of three counts of war crimes. Prosecutors had accused Said of presiding over the Central Office for the Repression of Banditry (OCRB) detention centre in the capital, Bangui, where prisoners were allegedly subjected to torture and severe deprivation. The court will determine Said’s sentence at a later date. The Central African Republic descended into civil war in 2013 after the mainly Muslim Seleka rebel coalition seized power, triggering widespread violence and reprisals between armed groups. AFP The post ICC convicts ex-CAR rebel leader for crimes against humanity appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: GRA’s ITAS and other digital platforms set to strengthen tax compliance
items.description: The Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) is deploying its Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS) to bring key aspects of the country’s tax administration onto a single digital platform, with the aim of improving taxpayer services, strengthening compliance, and enabling more effective use of data. Speaking during the latest instalment of the UK-Ghana Chamber of Commerce (UKGCC) and PwC Ghana’s Quarterly Tax Dialogue Series on “Navigating GRA’s Digital Tax Systems”, the Commissioner of the Domestic Tax Revenue Division, Dr. Martin Kolbil Yamborigya, said, “ITAS is a unified platform for the full tax cycle. It is part of GRA’s continued data transformation in line with international standards, replacing the separate legacy system with a single integrated tax administration system.” According to Dr. Yamborigya, the system will standardise processes across GRA offices, covering registration, filing, payment and taxpayer accounting, as well as compliance and risk management, audits, objections and appeals, exemptions, refund processing, debt management and investigations. Key benefits for taxpayers include self-service account activation, digital submission of applications and enquiries, automated workflows, online tracking of requests, fewer manual delays, risk-based audits, and the ability to authorise staff or tax consultants to act on behalf of businesses. To strengthen tax administration, ITAS will be linked to several national databases and platforms, including the Integrated Customs Management System (ICUMS), the Office of the Registrar of Companies, the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT), the Bank of Ghana, Ghana.gov, the Lands Commission and the National Identification Authority. Dr. Yamborigya urged businesses and taxpayers to embrace the system, noting that GRA’s goal is to reduce paperwork and automate processes to improve service delivery. Some ITAS capabilities are already operational, while additional features, including greater automation and pre-population of taxpayer information, will be progressively rolled out as implementation advances. Beyond ITAS: e-invoicing, Sentinel and informal sector taxation Beyond ITAS, the GRA outlined other digital initiatives aimed at improving compliance and broadening the tax net. One such initiative is the electronic invoicing (e-invoicing) system, which digitises the issuance and validation of invoices, debit notes and credit notes between suppliers and customers. The system authenticates invoices in real time, allowing GRA to validate transactions almost instantly. Dr. Yamborigya, however, emphasised that “e-invoicing is just an invoicing system and not a payment system”, explaining that it is intended to eliminate invoice forgery, reduce false input VAT claims, lower audit costs and improve compliance data for risk profiling. For businesses, he said the benefits include a fairer tax environment, simplified VAT returns, faster refunds, lower compliance costs and better record-keeping. He also explained the Sentinel project, which seeks to improve taxation of digital transactions. The initiative, introduced at the direction of the Ministry of Finance, is a digital tax collection and monitoring system aimed at enhancing digital tax transparency, improving VAT and levy collection, and streamlining cross-border digital transactions. Under the system, VAT is disclosed and collected at the point of payment through participating payment platforms. “Sentinel is simply a payment deduction platform and not meant to replace all other responsibilities,” Dr. Yamborigya explained, stressing that affected taxpayers will still be required to register where necessary and file tax returns. The Authority also highlighted the Modified Taxation Scheme for informal sector taxpayers whose annual turnover falls below the prescribed threshold, now increased to GH¢750,000. The scheme comprises three categories – presumptive tax based on instalment for businesses with turnover below GH¢20,000; presumptive tax based on turnover where taxpayers pay a flat three per cent of turnover and are not required to register for VAT; and modified cash basis which allows qualifying taxpayers who keep records to be taxed using simplified accounting principles. An accompanying mobile application allows taxpayers to register using their Ghana Card details and estimated turnover, after which the system automatically computes the applicable tax liability. Demystifying VAT refunds: what businesses need to know Addressing one of the most frequently raised concerns among businesses, Dr. Yamborigya explained the principles behind VAT refunds and the conditions required for a successful claim. “VAT is designed to be a tax on the final consumer and not on business input,” he said, noting that the refund mechanism protects VAT neutrality, supports exporters and businesses with persistent input credits, improves cash flow and strengthens confidence in the tax system. However, he cautioned that not every VAT credit is automatically refundable and stressed that a refund request must meet certain conditions before a refund can be applied. According to Dr. Yamborigya, taxpayers who qualify for VAT refunds include businesses generating excess input VAT, exporters with significant input VAT, businesses making zero-rated supplies, enterprises undertaking substantial capital expenditure and taxpayers with genuine VAT overpayments. Exporters qualify where exports account for at least 25 per cent of taxable supplies and appropriate documentation can be verified. For businesses seeking faster processing, he encouraged readiness by ensuring all VAT returns are filed, invoices and customs evidence are available, transactions are traceable, exports are supported by proper documentation and outstanding liabilities are reconciled before submission. “The stronger the evidence chain, the easier the verification for you,” he advised, and urged taxpayers to “ask not only how do I get a VAT refund. Ask, how do I ensure that my refund entitlement can be demonstrated quickly, accurately and conclusively”. A call for compliance and partnership Dr. Yamborigya encouraged businesses to maintain proper documentation, reconcile records consistently, understand statutory requirements, and embrace digital invoicing and electronic record-keeping, which are becoming increasingly central to tax administration. He further underscored GRA’s broader strategy of encouraging compliance through engagement and education. “Our objective is to move away from enforcement and penalties to a compliance regime. We believe that when taxpayers understand what is required of them, they’ll do the right thing,” he stated. The webinar, moderated by Laura Torgbenoo Fiagome, Associate Director, Tax Services at PwC Ghana, also explored practical issues including how taxpayers can identify and contact their assigned relationship managers, onboarding procedures for e-invoicing, methods for verifying genuine invoices through QR code validation, VAT compliance responsibilities, tax refund procedures and taxpayer support services.

items.title: La CBG maintient sa certification ASI Performance Standard V2 (2017)
items.description: Kamsar le 21 septembre 2026 – La Compagnie des Bauxites de Guinée (CBG) a obtenu le maintien de sa certification à l’ASI Performance Standard V2 de l’Aluminium Stewardship Initiative (ASI), à l’issue de son deuxième audit de surveillance réalisé du 22 au 30 juin 2026. Cette certification atteste de la conformité des opérations de la CBG aux exigences de la norme en matière de gouvernance, d’environnement, de droits humains, de santé et sécurité, de pratiques sociales et de relations avec les communautés. Une norme internationale pour une chaîne de valeur plus responsable L’Aluminium Stewardship Initiative (ASI) est une organisation internationale qui définit des standards de durabilité pour la chaîne de valeur de l’aluminium. L’ ASI Performance Standard V2 (2017) s’articule autour de principes couvrant notamment la gouvernance et la transparence, les émissions et la gestion environnementale, l’eau, la biodiversité, les droits humains, les conditions de travail ainsi que les relations avec les communautés. Pour la CBG, le maintien de cette certification vient reconnaître la continuité des actions engagées pour intégrer ces exigences dans ses opérations et faire progresser ses pratiques. Un périmètre qui couvre les principales opérations de la CBG Le périmètre certifié comprend notamment : La mine de Sangarédi Le chemin de fer reliant Sangarédi à Kamsar Les installations de traitement de la bauxite et les opérations portuaires à Kamsar Le site de compensation de biodiversité de Moyen-Bafing Ainsi que les infrastructures et activités associées couvertes par la certification. Cette couverture permet d’évaluer l’application des exigences ASI sur les différents maillons des opérations de la CBG, de la mine au port et dans les activités supports concernées. Une mobilisation collective Le maintien de la certification fait suite à plusieurs mois de préparation et à la mobilisation des équipes opérationnelles et des fonctions support. L’audit de surveillance a permis d’examiner les pratiques, les processus et les dispositifs mis en œuvre au regard des exigences de l’ASI Performance Standard. Pour Karifa Condé, Directeur Général de la CBG : « Le maintien de notre certification ASI vient reconnaître le travail accompli collectivement et les efforts déployés pour intégrer les exigences environnementales, sociales et de gouvernance dans nos activités. Je remercie l’ensemble de nos collaborateurs pour leur engagement et leur professionnalisme. Cette certification nous engage également à poursuivre nos efforts et à continuer d’améliorer nos pratiques. » Pour Oumar Sy, Chef Service Qualité de la CBG , cette étape traduit également le travail mené dans la durée : « Le maintien de la certification ASI est le résultat d’un travail rigoureux et d’une forte mobilisation des équipes. Au-delà de l’audit, cette démarche permet de renforcer nos processus, de faire progresser nos pratiques et d’ancrer davantage l’amélioration continue dans nos activités quotidiennes. » Poursuivre l’amélioration des pratiques Le maintien de la certification ASI Performance Standard V2 s’inscrit dans une démarche d’amélioration continue. La CBG poursuit ainsi les actions engagées dans les domaines de la gouvernance, de l’environnement, de la santé et de la sécurité, des droits humains et des relations avec les communautés. Cette étape prépare également la transition vers la Version 3 de l’ASI Performance Standard , prévue dans le cadre de la démarche de certification de la CBG en 2027. L’objectif reste de continuer à faire évoluer les pratiques de l’entreprise au regard des standards internationaux, tout en conciliant performance opérationnelle, responsabilité environnementale et sociale et création de valeur durable. À propos de la CBG La Compagnie des Bauxites de Guinée (CBG) est l’un des principaux producteurs de bauxite de qualité au monde. Fondée en 1963, la CBG est une coentreprise détenue à 49 % par l’État guinéen et à 51 % par le consortium Halco Mining, composé des groupes internationaux Alcoa, Rio Tinto et Dadco Investments. Acteur majeur de l’économie nationale, la CBG inscrit ses activités dans une logique de performance responsable, intégrant la sécurité, le développement durable et l’engagement communautaire. Présente depuis plus de cinq décennies, elle œuvre chaque jour à faire bien plus que de la bauxite.

items.title: You are no match for Peter Obi, leave him alone, Awuzie tells Umahi, Soludo
items.description: By Chidi Nkwopara OWERRI — Igbo leaders and the leadership of Ohanaeze Ndigbo have been urged to speak out against what has been described as continued attacks on the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, by some Igbo politicians. Former National President of the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Prof. Ukachukwu Awuzie, made the call while speaking with newsmen in Owerri. Awuzie specifically urged Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo and the Minister of Works, Engr. Dave Umahi, to focus on their respective responsibilities rather than attacking Obi’s record. He also expressed concern over what he described as the continued silence or apparent indifference of Igbo leaders to the exchanges involving the politicians. His words: “The patriotic Igbo man is known for speaking out. So, what are our Elders-in-Council in the South-East doing? What about those in Ohanaeze Ndigbo and those in Imeobi of Ohanaeze? “Why can’t they call Governor Soludo and Engr. Umahi to order? They should tell the duo to leave Obi alone.” Awuzie advised Soludo and Umahi to concentrate on their public responsibilities, saying attempts to discredit Obi’s record as governor would not succeed. “There should be a limit to greed, envy and jealousy. They should face governance; govern well and minister well. They can’t be a match to Obi, no matter how they try to rubbish his credibility. Igbo elders should rise and show leadership,” he said. The former ASUU president further described Obi as the kind of leader he believes Nigeria needs at the present time. “Obi is a kind of leader Nigeria wants at this point in time. He is a different breed of politician. So, if Nigerians know what is good for them, they should bank on Mr. Peter Obi,” he said. Awuzie also dismissed suggestions that comments by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his supporters could damage Obi’s reputation. “No matter what President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his stooges do or say, they will not succeed in putting a dent on the integrity, character and personality of Mr. Peter Obi,” he said. He described Obi as a model and said he believed many Nigerians, beyond the South-East, were proud of him. “Obi is a model and somebody Ndigbo are proud of and I believe that other Nigerians are also proud of him. This is because, wherever he goes across the country, people troop out to welcome him,” Awuzie added. The post You are no match for Peter Obi, leave him alone, Awuzie tells Umahi, Soludo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘I hope to dedicate Ballon d’Or to Africa if I win’ — Mbappe
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye France captain Kylian Mbappé says he hopes to dedicate the Ballon d’Or to Africa if he wins the prestigious individual award next month, stressing that he has never cut ties with his African roots. The Real Madrid forward, whose father is Cameroonian and mother is of Algerian descent, made the remarks in an interview with RFI, saying his African upbringing remains an important part of his identity despite representing France throughout his football career. “I’ve always had an upbringing steeped in African culture, even though I was born in France and did everything in France,” Mbappe said. “I have never cut ties with my roots, my origins. It’s part of the values instilled in you.” Mbappe has increasingly embraced his African roots publicly and visited Cameroon in July 2023, travelling to Yaounde before visiting Douala and Djebale, the island where his father’s family is from. The visit also included trips to schools supported by his foundation and a meeting with Prime Minister Joseph Dion Ngu. “I went back to Cameroon not long ago,” he told RFI. “I used to go there when I was little, I had an amazing time. Every time I go to Africa, I’m always welcomed so warmly, I feel the love from people.” Despite his African heritage, Mbappe said there had never been any doubt about his decision to represent France. “I was born in France, I am French, I did everything in France,” he said earlier this year. “I have Cameroonian and Algerian origins, but I grew up with French culture.” With voting for the 2026 Ballon d’Or approaching, Mbappe is among the nominees for the men’s award and is hoping to receive support from across Africa. The winner will be crowned at a ceremony in London on October 26. A victory would place him alongside Eusebio, George Weah, Zinedine Zidane, Karim Benzema and Ousmane Dembélé among players of African origin who have won the prize. “First off, I thank them for the support over all these years,” he said. “I’ve always felt so loved every time I’ve set foot on the African continent. I think that, having African origins, it’s always a pleasure when people associate me with the Ballon d’Or. “I thank them for everything and I hope to leave with the Ballon d’Or, and in one way or another, dedicate it to them.” Mbappe is seeking the first Ballon d’Or of his career after another prolific season with Real Madrid and a standout FIFA World Cup with France. He scored 25 goals to finish as La Liga’s leading scorer in 2025-26, added 15 in the Champions League and another two in the Copa del Rey, finishing the season with 42 goals in 44 appearances for Real Madrid. The post ‘I hope to dedicate Ballon d’Or to Africa if I win’ — Mbappe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: How school support is helping parents in Ejura Sekyedumasi prepare children for senior high school
items.description: Regina Appiah had been thinking about how she would provide the things her child needed to start senior high school because she did not have the money to buy the required items. “I cannot afford these items. I do not have the money,” said Mrs Appiah. She was among parents in Ejura Sekyedumasi who received school supplies provided by the Member of Parliament, Bawah Muhammed Braimah, for students preparing to enter senior high school. The package has helped Mrs Appiah meet some of the costs she was struggling to cover, and she believes the support will help her child continue his education. “These items will help secure my child’s future. I will be able to enrol my child in school, and I believe he will become great in the future, for me and for the country,” she said. She thanked the MP, the District Chief Executive and other community leaders for the assistance and expressed the hope that similar support would be available to families in the constituency in the future. “I pray that God protects our Honourable Member of Parliament so that, God willing, he will do the same thing again next year,” she said. Franklina Sarpong was also concerned about how she would provide some of the basic items her niece needed for school, particularly a trunk and a chop box, which she could not afford at the time. “I did not have money to buy a chop box and trunks. I had been worried about that for some time, but, God willing, I have now received a trunk, chop box, mattress, books and other items,” she said. She said the support would allow her to keep some of the little money she has for other things her niece may need. “Now I can manage the little money I have and use it to buy some of the smaller things my child needs,” she said. Franklina said providing everything the children needed for school had been difficult for her family. “When the children completed school, we did not have enough money to provide everything they needed,” she said. She said she was particularly grateful for the trunk, chop box, rubber and the other items she received. Why the support was introduced Mr Braimah said the programme was introduced because parents still have to provide basic items when their children enter senior high school, even though tuition is covered under Ghana’s Free SHS programme. “We know that we have Free SHS education, but when it is time for children to go to school, most parents are unable to provide them with the necessary items on the school prospectus, such as metal trunks, mattresses, pillows and other essentials,” he said. The MP said 500 students are being supported this year with metal trunks, mattresses, pillows, exercise books and buckets. Students who obtained aggregates from six to nine were automatic beneficiaries, he said, while the best students in their respective schools were also included. Mr Braimah said the selection was also intended to encourage other students to work harder. “I believe this will motivate the rest of the students to study hard so that, next time, they can also benefit from the package we are providing,” he said. He described the programme as his contribution towards supporting students entering secondary school. “We are putting this together as our widow’s mite to support students who are going to secondary school,” he said. The cost of preparing for school Mr Braimah said some students who qualify for senior high school can still struggle to begin their education because their parents cannot afford the basic supplies required by the schools. “We have realised that, in some cases, students who qualify to go to senior high school are unable to do so because their parents cannot afford some of these basic items,” he said. He said a complete set of the items being provided to each student was worth more than GH¢1,000. “We expect that this support will go a long way to help these children in their education so that they can grow up to become useful members of society,” he said. For Mrs Appiah, the assistance has helped her provide items she says she could not have bought herself. Franklina said she was equally grateful for the support. “I am truly happy to have received these items. It is not everywhere that you get this kind of support, and not everyone gets it,” she said.

items.title: Why public universities might start charging N1m tuition fee – LASU ex-VC
items.description: Former Vice Chancellor of Lagos State University, Ibiyemi Olatunji-Bello, has said public universities in Nigeria may need to charge at least N1 million per student annually to achieve financial sustainability. Olatunji-Bello, whose five-year tenure ended on Saturday, made the comment in an exclusive interview with Punch. She identified inadequate funding as one of the major challenges facing public universities, noting that LASU’s internally generated revenue had grown significantly but remained insufficient to meet its financial obligations. According to the former vice chancellor, LASU currently spends more than N1 billion monthly on salaries, while its annual internally generated revenue stands at about N13 billion. “Universities can achieve financial self-sustainability. If they can innovate and ensure improvements in the institution, money will come in,” she said. “But then, if the money comes in, how do you spend it? Right now, LASU does not have financial self-sustainability. “Our payroll right now is over N1 billion per month. All the N13 billion IGR does not cover our salaries.” Olatunji-Bello said universities seeking financial independence would therefore have to significantly increase their tuition fees. “So, universities that want to attain self-sustainability will have to increase school fees into millions,” she said. She added that some secondary schools already charge more than N1 million per term, while some public universities still collect around N100,000 annually. “So, any public university that wants to sustain financial independence will have to charge school fees of not less than N1 million per student,” the former vice chancellor said. Olatunji-Bello also stressed that maintaining quality education requires substantial funding, urging parents to prioritise the education of their children. “Good quality education needs money,” she said. During her five-year tenure, Olatunji-Bello said LASU increased its internally generated revenue from about N3 billion to N13 billion through new programmes, digital initiatives and other revenue-generating efforts. She identified a 2024 Students’ Union protest over a N10,000 payment for computer-based testing as the lowest point of her administration. However, she described LASU’s emergence as the most subscribed university among UTME candidates in 2025 as one of the major highlights of her tenure. “When JAMB declared that we were the most subscribed university by UTME candidates in Nigeria; that was great for me,” she said. “And this year, 2026, we maintained that number one position. And not only did we maintain it, but we were even awarded N25 million for maintaining compliance with JAMB regulations.” The post Why public universities might start charging N1m tuition fee – LASU ex-VC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Government to resume Dome–Kitase road works, targets completion by 2028
items.description: The government has decided to resume construction of the Dome–Kitase Road that links the Greater Accra and Eastern regions under its Big Push Infrastructure Programme, the Ministry of Roads and Highways has announced. In a social media post, the ministry said Roads and Highways Minister Kwame Agbodza had directed the contractor, First Sky Limited, to fully mobilise to the site by the end of this week. Work on the project stalled following Ghana’s debt restructuring programme in 2022, when it was approximately 27 per cent complete. Under the current arrangement, the road is expected to be finished by the end of 2028. The ministry said the project’s scope had been expanded to include 10 kilometres of connecting roads to nearby communities, with the aim of improving access and connectivity. “We are taking the necessary steps to ensure that this project resumes fully and progresses without interruption. The contractor is expected to mobilise back to site by the end of this week, and we want to see sustained work until the project is completed,” Mr Agbodza said. According to the ministry, the decision to prioritise the road is part of the government’s wider effort to address infrastructure needs across the country.

items.title: ‘Ghana Jollof’ Case: High Court adjourns Salomey Baffoe’s bail application hearing to Sept. 24
items.description: The High Court in Accra has adjourned to September 24 the hearing of a bail application filed on behalf of Salomey Baffoe, who is accused of abetting the publication of false information by a social media account under the name ‘Ghana Jollof’ on TikTok. The adjournment followed a request by the prosecution for additional time to respond to the defence’s application for bail. Assistant State Attorney Carl Afedzi Forson told the court that he was not the substantive lawyer handling the case and had been informed that the Attorney-General’s Office was served with the bail application last Friday. He explained that Monday was a public holiday and, consequently, the application had not yet been assigned to a lawyer within the office for a response. The prosecution therefore asked the court for a short adjournment to enable the State to prepare and file its response. Counsel for Baffoe, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, opposed the request, arguing that the application concerned the liberty of his client and should not be treated in the same manner as a civil proceeding where parties are required to observe three clear days for service. He maintained that there was evidence that the prosecution had been served with the application and noted that the State had not claimed it had been short-served. According to the defence, applications involving the liberty of an accused person could be heard even over weekends, meaning the relevant period for the State to respond should continue to run despite the public holiday on Monday. Mr Awuah further argued that the prosecution had had sufficient time to respond to the application. He cautioned that further delays could undermine the purpose of the bail application, particularly as Baffoe would have spent about two weeks in custody by the time the State filed and served its response. In its ruling on the adjournment request, the court acknowledged that the liberty of the applicant was at stake and stressed that the State could not take the matter for granted. The court subsequently adjourned the bail application to September 24. It directed the Republic to file any processes it intended to rely on and serve them on the defence by 9:00 a.m. on the scheduled date. Baffoe remains in custody pending the determination of her bail application.

items.title: You have no right to govern other countries, Brazilian President tells Trump
items.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has told United States President Donald Trump that he has no right to impose his will on other countries, arguing that nations should be allowed to protect their sovereignty and pursue their own interests. Lula made the remarks in an exclusive interview with CNN’s Christiane Amanpour ahead of the ongoing United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York. The Brazilian president said Trump’s approach to international relations appeared to be based on the idea that the strongest country should dictate terms to others. “President Trump was elected to be the US president. He has the right to govern the US, but he doesn’t have the right to govern other countries,” Lula said. “He doesn’t have the right to impose his will. He has to have the willingness to negotiate.” Lula said every country had the right to determine its own affairs, adding that the United States should not impose its rules on other nations. “We just want to say that every country has their own sovereignty. They take care of their own interests and the US cannot impose their rules over the others,” he said. The Brazilian leader also criticised tariffs imposed by the Trump administration on Brazilian imports. According to the account of the interview, the United States imposed a 25 per cent tariff on certain Brazilian goods in July following an investigation by the US Trade Representative. Washington said the measures were in response to what it described as Brazilian policies affecting digital trade, electronic payments, intellectual property, ethanol market access, anti-corruption enforcement and illegal deforestation. Lula rejected the justification for the tariffs, describing them as based on “lies”, and said Brazil had responded by seeking to strengthen trade relations with other countries. He said Brazil’s exports to the US had fallen by nine per cent, while imports from the US declined by 8.5 per cent following the tariffs. Lula also cited increased trade with China, Japan, Germany and the European Union. “So I’m not going to just try to cry out about the milk that was spilled on the floor. I’m going to seek other partners to try to buy and sell,” he said. Lula added that Brazil was still negotiating with the US and would consider retaliatory measures only if the talks failed. “I don’t want to go to a tariff war with the US and neither with any other country,” he said. Lula warns against election interference The Brazilian president also expressed concern about possible US interference in Brazil’s elections, while acknowledging that there was no concrete evidence. Lula said there were “some clues” involving interference and artificial intelligence, and mentioned US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s relationship with the Bolsonaro family. “But for the meanwhile, we just have suspicion. There’s nothing concrete,” he said. Lula criticises US role in Venezuela Lula also criticised the Trump administration’s role in Venezuela, saying Washington’s actions had created the impression that the United States was governing the South American country. The comments followed the US military operation that resulted in the capture of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in January and the subsequent emergence of Delcy Rodríguez as interim president. Reuters reported earlier this month that Rodríguez was leading Venezuela’s interim government and had been engaging with US officials on economic and energy matters. “The US conveys the idea that they’re governing Venezuela,” Lula said. “Every document that we read, the agreements, it looks like the US is the big boss of Venezuela, the sovereignty of the country has ended.” Lula said the situation was not good for Venezuela, the United States or democracy, arguing that Venezuelans should be allowed to determine their political future through elections. “If I was Delcy, the president, I would call for election, national election, so that people could choose who’s going to be the next president of the country,” he said. Lula’s comments come as Trump has continued to defend an expanded US role in Venezuela and the wider Western Hemisphere. In his September 22 address to the UN General Assembly, Trump cited the Venezuela operation while calling for greater US military dominance in the region. The post You have no right to govern other countries, Brazilian President tells Trump appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Asafo Market baby theft: Police search for suspect after granting her bail; family wants answers
items.description: Uncertainty is growing over the case of a five-month-old baby boy allegedly stolen at Asafo Market in Kumasi after fresh developments emerged. The prime suspect, whose identity has yet to be disclosed, was reportedly arrested at Ejisu but has since been granted police enquiry bail, a development that has raised questions among family members following conflicting accounts about her arrest and release. The baby was reportedly stolen from the Cape Coast Bus Terminal section of the Asafo Market, specifically an area known as Opera Site, in the early hours of Sunday, September 20, 2026. The traumatised parents, Freda Owusu and her husband, Emmanuel Acheampong, immediately lodged a formal complaint at the Asokwa Police Station on the day of the incident, prompting the police to launch a manhunt. Two days after the incident, the case took a dramatic turn. Speaking to JoyNews on Tuesday, September 22, Mr Osei Kuffour, an uncle of the missing child, disclosed that the family received a tip-off around 4:00 p.m. on Monday, September 21, that police at Ejisu had arrested a woman travelling with a baby. He explained that, according to the information received, the woman had boarded a VIP bus heading towards Accra, but her interaction with the infant aroused the suspicion of other passengers. Upon reaching Ejisu, the passengers reportedly lodged a complaint at the Ejisu Divisional Police Command, leading to her arrest. In an effort to verify the information, relatives of the missing child went to the Ejisu police station, where officers on duty reportedly confirmed that a woman with an infant in her custody had been arrested on suspicion of child stealing but had subsequently been released. “When we went to the Ejisu police station to confirm, the officers on duty admitted that a woman with a baby was arrested over claims of child stealing, but she had already been released,” Mr Kuffour said. He alleged that the police released the woman after a man appeared at the station claiming to be her husband and insisting that the baby belonged to them. Mr Kuffour said the family was told by the police to return home and report back on Tuesday, September 22, as efforts were being made to re-arrest the suspect. “They told us to go home and come back on Tuesday as they are intensifying efforts to bring the suspect back, but unfortunately, when we went back to the police today, the suspect and her husband didn’t show up,” he lamented. Responding to the development, the Ejisu Divisional Police Commander, Chief Superintendent Samuel Kofi Gamson, confirmed the arrest and subsequent release of the woman. He clarified that the suspect was arrested on Sunday and was granted bail in line with police procedures. “She was arrested on Sunday and remained in police custody overnight before being granted bail. During that time, no official baby theft case had been filed by anyone,” he said. Chief Supt Gamson assured that efforts were underway to locate and bring in the woman, the baby and the man who allegedly presented himself as her husband to secure her bail for further investigations. “They are in Accra, so I have sent my officers to go there and bring the suspect woman, the baby and the husband, so that we can conduct an identification parade to see if truly she stole the baby or not,” he said. He said the identification parade would be crucial in determining whether the child in the woman’s custody was indeed the missing child. “By 11 a.m. tomorrow, I am expecting them to arrive so we can continue investigations into the matter from there,” Chief Supt Gamson stated.

items.title: Dr Fatou Sanogo : « les droits des femmes ne doivent pas seulement exister dans les lois, ils doivent aussi être connus et respectés dans nos communautés »
items.description: À travers « Les violences d’une vie de femme », un spectacle prévu le 26 septembre à Kuma So, à Bamako, Dr Fatou Sanogo, médecin de santé publique, artiste slameuse et cofondatrice d’ORATIO, veut raconter autrement les blessures visibles et invisibles vécues par de nombreuses femmes. Dans cet entretien accordé à notre rédaction, elle revient sur cette création artistique qui mêle slam, théâtre, chant et danse, son engagement en faveur des droits des femmes et son ambition de faire voyager ce message dans plusieurs pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest. Mediaguinee : Le 26 septembre à Kuma So, vous présentez « Les violences d'une vie de femme ». Pouvez-vous vous présenter et nous expliquer de quelles violences parle ce spectacle ? Dr Fatou Sanogo : Dr Fatou SANOGO, médecin de santé publique et artiste slameuse. Je suis également Co-fondatrice et directrice d'ORATIO, une structure à travers laquelle nous développons des initiatives qui placent l'humain au cœur de la santé et de la transformation sociale. Les violences d'une vie de femme » est une création artistique qui raconte l'histoire de Hawa, une femme de 60 ans qui, après le décès de son mari, revient sur les différentes étapes de sa vie. À travers son histoire, nous abordons l'excision, le mariage précoce, les violences conjugales, la polygamie et la privation de certains droits. Mais nous parlons aussi de ces violences qui ne se voient pas toujours : les rêves abandonnés, les choix imposés et les souffrances que certaines femmes portent en silence pendant des années. Mediaguinee : Pourquoi avoir choisi d'associer le slam, le théâtre, le chant et la danse pour porter ce message ? Dr Fatou Sanogo : Au-delà d’être médecin, je suis aussi une femme profondément attachée à l'art et à la force de la parole. Dans notre travail de sensibilisation, nous utilisons souvent des chiffres, des données et des messages de prévention. Ils sont essentiels, mais ils ne suffisent pas toujours à toucher les personnes. L'art nous permet d'aborder ces mêmes réalités autrement, avec plus de proximité et d'émotion. Le slam donne une voix à Hawa, le théâtre nous permet de vivre son histoire, tandis que le chant et l'expression corporelle accompagnent les émotions qu'elle traverse. Nous avons voulu créer un spectacle qui invite le public à ressentir, à comprendre et à réfléchir, sans jugement. Mediaguinee : Ce spectacle est-il inspiré de faits réels, de témoignages de femmes africaines ? Dr Fatou Sanogo : Hawa est un personnage de fiction, mais les réalités qu'elle traverse sont bien réelles. Son histoire fait écho à celle de nombreuses femmes africaines qui, à différentes étapes de leur vie, ont été confrontées à des violences ou à des situations dans lesquelles elles n'ont pas toujours eu la possibilité de faire leurs propres choix. Nous avons choisi de raconter une seule vie pour mettre en lumière ces différentes réalités. Mediaguinee : En 2003, les États africains ont adopté le Protocole de Maputo pour renforcer la protection des droits des femmes. Plus de vingt ans après, comment votre spectacle peut-il contribuer à faire de ces engagements une réalité dans nos communautés ? Dr Fatou Sanogo : Le Protocole de Maputo représente une avancée importante dans la reconnaissance et la protection des droits des femmes africaines. Plusieurs États, dont la Guinée et le Mali, l'ont ratifié. Mais au-delà de la ratification, il y a la domestication, c'est-à-dire l'intégration de ces engagements dans nos législations nationales, et surtout leur mise en œuvre effective. Certaines dispositions sont déjà présentes dans nos législations, mais leur application reste parfois difficile. Les droits des femmes ne doivent pas seulement exister dans les lois, ils doivent aussi être connus et respectés dans nos communautés. Je suis convaincue que les lois doivent s'accompagner d'un travail de sensibilisation et de dialogue. C'est tout le sens de notre création. À travers l'histoire de Hawa, nous souhaitons ouvrir le dialogue, faire connaître les droits des femmes et inviter chacun à contribuer à leur protection. Mediaguinee : Après cette représentation au Mali, vous souhaitez porter ce spectacle dans plusieurs pays d'Afrique de l'Ouest. Quelles sont vos ambitions et quel appel souhaitez-vous lancer ? Dr Fatou Sanogo : Les violences d'une vie de femme » est une création portée par ORATIO et Art Academy du Mali. Notre ambition est de poursuivre cette aventure artistique et humaine en Guinée, en Côte d'Ivoire, au Burkina Faso, au Sénégal… La Guinée occupe une place toute particulière dans mon cœur, puisque c'est mon pays d'origine. J'aimerais profondément que nous puissions y présenter ce spectacle et partager cette histoire avec nos communautés. Aujourd'hui, nous souhaitons lancer un appel aux institutions publiques, aux partenaires techniques et financiers, aux entreprises et aux organisations engagées dans la promotion des droits des femmes. Nous avons une équipe artistique mobilisée, une création à partager et un message qui mérite d'être entendu au-delà des frontières. Nous avons besoin de partenaires pour rendre cette tournée possible, mais aussi pour accompagner les échanges et les actions de sensibilisation qui pourront prolonger chaque représentation. Mediaguinee : Un dernier mot à vos invités ? Dr Fatou Sanogo : Je voudrais tout simplement vous inviter à venir découvrir « Les violences d'une vie de femme », le 26 septembre à Kuma So, à Bamako.Venez écouter l'histoire de Hawa, une histoire qui pourrait faire écho à celle de votre mère, de votre sœur, de votre épouse ou de votre fille. Christine Finda Kamano L’article Dr Fatou Sanogo : « les droits des femmes ne doivent pas seulement exister dans les lois, ils doivent aussi être connus et respectés dans nos communautés » est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Yamal: Ballon d’Or not decided by number of goals
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal has said the Ballon d’Or should not be decided by the number of goals a player scores, but by the player who brings the most joy to football fans. Yamal made the remarks in an interview with L’Equipe, as he remains in contention for this year’s award after finishing second to Ousmane Dembélé last year. The 19-year-old is among the leading contenders for the prize, alongside Dembélé, Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé and Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane. The winner will be crowned at a ceremony in London on October 26. Yamal said the presence of several contenders had created more debate, with the final decision resting with journalists. “It’s fun that there are more players [up for the prize], more debate and people can have different opinions,” Yamal told L’Equipe. “At the end of the day, it comes down to the journalists. It’s a difficult job for them. We all have good arguments to win it. We are all great players, so let’s see. “The Ballon d’Or is for the best player of the year, someone different, someone we have enjoyed watching, who has that magic, makes you smile and look forward to watching games just to see them play. “It’s not to do with the sheer number of goals. When I think of the Ballon d’Or, I think of [Lionel] Messi, Ronaldinho… different players, players that make you dream.” Kane scored 61 goals for Bayern, who won the Bundesliga, while Mbappé scored 42 for Real Madrid without winning a trophy last season. Yamal scored 24 goals, while Dembélé scored 20 for Paris Saint-Germain, who won the European title. Yamal also believes his style of play and his success with Spain strengthen his case for the award. “On the pitch I enjoy myself,” he added. “I have also been lucky enough to win a lot of trophies with Barcelona. “And I won the biggest trophy of them all, the World Cup with my national team. But beyond all that, I think the way I play is the strongest argument and what makes me different.” Yamal, still a teenager, has already won the European Championships and World Cup with Spain, while the Champions League remains the only major team trophy he is yet to win. He admitted that winning the Ballon d’Or is one of his ambitions, but said he does not regard it as an obsession. “Yes, I dream of winning [the Ballon d’Or],” he said. “I always say that everyone has to aim as high as possible. If I was a waiter, I would want to own the restaurant. “I play to make history, so that in 30 years kids say: ‘He was really good.’ But it’s not an obsession. I never think ‘I want to be better than Pele or Messi.’ I don’t want to compare myself with others. “I want to be Lamine Yamal. I want to be remembered as Lamine Yamal. I hope to be remembered among the greats. I have the capacity to do it; it depends on me.” Meanwhile, Kane’s Bayern teammate Luis Díaz backed the England striker as his choice for the award in an interview with ESPN. “I already knew he scored loads of goals, but training with him every day, seeing his mentality, he has dazzled me even more,” Díaz said. “It’s difficult to sum him up in one word. Brutal, maybe… magnificent. For me, it’s hard to find the perfect word to describe him. “For me, he’s the No.1 candidate to win the Ballon d’Or. I hope he wins it.” The post Yamal: Ballon d’Or not decided by number of goals appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Lagos seals church, 11 others over environmental violations
items.description: LAGOS — The Lagos State Environmental Protection Agency (LASEPA) has sealed 12 establishments, including a church, across parts of the state over alleged persistent violations of environmental regulations. LASEPA disclosed this on its official X platform on Wednesday, following an enforcement operation carried out on Tuesday, September 22, 2026. The affected establishments, located in Ogba, Idimu-Ikota, Ejigbo, LASU-Iba Road, Igando and Agodo-Egbe areas, were reportedly sealed despite repeated warnings, abatement notices and opportunities granted to facilitate compliance with the agency’s directives. LASEPA said the enforcement exercise was carried out in line with the directives of the Lagos State Government to ensure compliance with environmental laws, safeguard public health and promote a cleaner and safer environment. According to the agency, the establishments were found to have violated various environmental regulations and failed to implement prescribed corrective measures or comply with directives issued by LASEPA. The establishments sealed include Thrillz Lounge, Odusanmi Street, Ogba, for noise pollution and non-compliance; Feixiang Plastic, LASU-Ojo Road, Oko Filling Bus Stop, for non-compliance; and Marvel Hotel & Suites, Chrisbee Crescent, BRT Bus Stop, Igando, for noise pollution and non-compliance. Also sealed were Keviz Hotel & Suites, Councilor Ajayi Street, Obadore Bus Stop, LASU-Iba Road, for obstruction of duty and non-compliance; DSN Hotel & Suites, Benson Onyeacholen Street, O’Mark Bus Stop, LASU-Igando Road; and Rudaj Vegetable Oil, Tanimowo Street, Ologufe Bus Stop, Igando Road, for non-compliance. The agency also sealed the Celestial Church of Christ (Aduragbemi Parish), Adetola Buhari Street, Okerube Bus Stop, Ikotun, for noise pollution and non-compliance with its directives. Others are Limas, Aro-Oloye Street, off Abaranje Road, Abaranje, Ikotun; Nico Hotel & Suites, Ayawo Close, NEPA Bus Stop, Egbe-Isolo Road, Ejigbo; and 10Kobo Night Club, Abanishe Street, off Hostel Road, Agodo-Egbe. While Limas and Nico Hotel & Suites were sealed for non-compliance, 10Kobo Night Club was cited for noise pollution and non-compliance. Master Furniture, Coleman Street, Pao Bus Stop, Idimu-Ikota Road, and Nikky’s Executive Bar & Lounge, Governor’s Road, Ikotun, were also sealed for non-compliance with the agency’s directives. Speaking on the enforcement operation, LASEPA General Manager, Dr. Babatunde Ajayi, reaffirmed the agency’s commitment to protecting public health and preserving the environment through sustained monitoring, regulatory compliance and enforcement of environmental standards across the state. Ajayi said environmental compliance was a collective responsibility, stressing that LASEPA would continue to intensify enforcement against individuals, businesses, religious organisations and corporate bodies whose activities pose risks to the environment, public health and the wellbeing of Lagos residents. He urged business owners, facility operators, religious institutions, scrap dealers and residents across the state to adopt environmentally responsible practices, obtain all necessary permits and approvals, and comply fully with applicable environmental regulations. He also called for cooperation with LASEPA in its efforts to build a cleaner, healthier and more sustainable Lagos.
